The figure on this page is a div. Its caption is the div's last
paragraph:

```markdown
::: {#fig-groups .wrap-left width="35%"}
![](groups.png)

Scores by hours of practice in two groups.
:::
```

## Result

Each participant practiced for some number of hours and then took a test.
The figure in this section plots each test score against the hours of
practice, with one color for each of the two groups. This paragraph comes
before the figure, so it runs the full width of the text.

::: {#fig-groups .wrap-left width="35%"}
![](../images/groups.png)

Scores by hours of practice in two groups.
:::

@fig-groups shows each participant's score against the hours that they
practiced. Scores rose with practice in both groups, and the second group
practiced more hours.

The class `.wrap-left` puts the figure on the left side of the text, so
this text flows on its right. The figure is 35% of the text width, a
little narrower than the default of 40%. The div form puts the caption in
its own paragraph, which is easier to read and edit when the caption is
long. The figure keeps its number, so the text can point to it. The lines
of this paragraph start beside the figure. After the text passes the
bottom of the figure, each line starts at the left edge of the text again
and runs under the figure. The text reads as one block around the figure,
not as two columns side by side. Wrapping goes on in this way until the
next block that is not a paragraph, such as the heading below.

## Next

A heading is not a paragraph, so wrapping stops before it.
